extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled by collecting 9 existing multimodal MathQA datasets, reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and selecting 19 publicly available math-related ones using heuristic rules plus expert manual labeling, and creating 3 new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) with manual annotation and review.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations because annotations were sourced from original data providers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from 31 source datasets: 9 existing MathQA datasets, 19 existing VQA datasets, and 3 newly annotated datasets; new data were sourced from online learning platforms and papers released on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was capped at up to 400 examples for balance; VQA candidates were heuristically filtered for likely mathematical reasoning; the benchmark was split into testmini and test using random sampling designed to preserve source distribution.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples likely involving mathematical reasoning by choosing examples with numeric answers or quantity words in questions; false positives were then manually filtered by expert annotators. Quality checks were also conducted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata such as question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning types. For new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and reviewed by three reviewers, with disagreements resolved by discussion. For VQA filtering, three expert annotators labeled whether examples involved mathematical reasoning, using majority voting.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was assessed via inter-annotation consistency and agreement metrics. New datasets had 99.2% inter-annotation consistency, with 6 disagreements among 736 questions resolved by team discussion. For mathematical reasoning labeling, automatic vs human annotations matched exactly on 94.1% of examples and 98.79% of individual labels. For mathematical-problem labeling, Fleiss' Kappa was 0.775.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; expert annotators; qualified human annotators with a high school diploma or higher for human baseline; AMT annotators with more than 5,000 HITs and acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules for automatic selection; automatic annotation for coarse mathematical reasoning labels
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Test answers will not be publicly released to prevent contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained; the authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard with new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support development of AI assistants for mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, including education, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Annotations come from heterogeneous original data providers and lack a unified format and structure; some source datasets may be underrepresented due to coverage gaps.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may have gaps in coverage of mathematical problems and visuals; collecting high-quality data is labor-intensive and may limit scalability and generalizability; only 85.6% of examples have annotations; annotations are heterogeneous and not unified.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of foundation models for mathematical reasoning in visual contexts; testmini is intended for model development validation or limited compute, and test is for standard evaluation.
